::: {.callout-important}
## Collect this brief at the Day 2 morning recap
Forty-five minutes is enough to *build* but not to *decide*. Read your
group's question over lunch, agree on who does what, and arrive at 15:15
ready to type.
:::

## The task

In 45 minutes, produce **one rendered Quarto document** (HTML or Word)
answering your group's question, containing:

| | Requirement |
|---|---|
| ☐ | A title, your names, and a two-sentence background |
| ☐ | A `gtsummary` table, properly labelled |
| ☐ | One labelled figure, saved with `ggsave()` |
| ☐ | At least one number reported through **inline code** |
| ☐ | A statement of how missing data were handled, with the count |
| ☐ | One honest limitation |
| ☐ | An AI disclosure sentence, or a statement that none was used |

Then present it in **four minutes**. Not the code — the finding, and one thing
that surprised you.

## Group questions

::: {.callout-note}
## Group 1 — Does attendance explain the effect?
The flipped classroom arm gains more. Is that because of the teaching method,
or because those students attended more?

Compare attendance between arms, then look at whether the gain difference
survives adjustment for attendance. Report both the unadjusted and adjusted
estimates in one table.

*Verbs you will need:* `group_by()`, `summarise()`, `lm()`,
`tbl_regression()`, `tbl_merge()`.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Group 2 — Which OSCE stations discriminate?
Using `osce_stations.csv`, find which stations separate strong from weak
students and which do not.

For each station, compute the mean, SD, and the correlation between station
score and OSCE total. A station that correlates poorly with the total is
measuring something else — or nothing.

*Verbs you will need:* `group_by()`, `summarise()`, `left_join()`, `cor()`,
`ggplot2` with `fct_reorder()`.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Group 3 — Is burnout related to performance?
Examine the relationship between `burnout_score`, `attendance_pct` and
`posttest`.

Beware the direction of causation: burnout may reduce attendance, attendance
may reduce burnout, or a third factor may drive both. Your document must state
which direction you can and cannot support with these cross-sectional data.

*Verbs you will need:* `filter()`, `mutate()` with `case_when()`,
`ggplot2` with `geom_smooth()`, `tbl_summary()` by `burnout_band`.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Group 4 — What do faculty say they need?
Clean `faculty_survey_raw.csv` and describe what it shows about faculty
research practice.

Cleaning is most of the work here: names, duplicates, inconsistent
departments, mixed missing-value codes. Report how many rows you started with,
how many you ended with, and why.

*Verbs you will need:* `janitor::clean_names()`, `distinct()`, `str_trim()`,
`str_to_title()`, `case_when()`, `count()`, `tbl_summary()`.
:::

## Starter document

Download [`report_template.qmd`](../R/report_template.qmd), or copy this:

````markdown
---
title: "Group N — your question here"
author: "Member A, Member B, Member C"
date: today
format:
  html: {toc: true, embed-resources: true}
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

```{{r}}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

students <- read_csv("data/meded_students.csv")
osce     <- read_csv("data/osce_stations.csv")
```

## Background

Two sentences: what was studied and why your question matters.

## Methods

Data from 240 students across three colleges (synthetic, for training).
Post-test scores were missing for
`r knitr::inline_expr("sum(is.na(students$posttest))")` students, who were
excluded from analyses of knowledge gain.

As shown in @tbl-main and @fig-main, ...

## Limitations

One honest paragraph.
````

`embed-resources: true` bundles images into a single HTML file — you can email
it, and it still works.

## How to split 45 minutes across a group of six

| Minutes | Everyone |
|---|---|
| 0–5 | Agree the answer you expect. Write it down. Compare later. |
| 5–20 | Two people write the analysis code; two draft the prose; two build the table |
| 20–30 | Merge into one `.qmd`. This always takes longer than expected |
| 30–40 | Render. Fix. Render again |
| 40–45 | Decide who presents and rehearse the four minutes once |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Render early, render often
Do not write for 40 minutes then render. Render at minute 10 with an empty
skeleton, and again every few minutes. A document that has never rendered
will fail at 15:58, and the failure will be a missing bracket.
:::

## Presentations {#presentations}

**16:15 – 17:00.** Four minutes per group, two minutes of questions.

Cover, in order:

1. Your question, in one sentence.
2. Your answer, in one sentence.
3. Your table or figure — on screen, from your rendered document.
4. What surprised you, or what you could not do.

::: {.callout-note}
## What we are assessing — and what we are not
**We are not assessing** statistical sophistication, elegance of code, or
whether you found a "significant" result.

**We are assessing** whether the document regenerates itself, whether the
numbers in the prose come from the data rather than from typing, and whether
you have been honest about what you do not know.

A group that reports "we found nothing, and here is why our design could not
have detected it" is doing better science than a group that found a p-value
below 0.05 in the fourth subgroup they tried.
:::

**Post-test, feedback and valedictory** — SET Team.

Please fill it in honestly, including the parts that did not work. The next
cohort inherits your answers.

## After the workshop

- Everything on this site stays online.
- The repository is public. Fork it, adapt it, run it in your own department.
- Bring your own data to the follow-up session — details circulated by email.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
## The one thing to take away
You will forget the syntax. Everyone does, and it is looked up in seconds.
What should survive is the habit: **one project folder, one script per step,
one source document, and a restart before you believe anything.**
:::
